data.name: About_ArchitectureBody
data.value: This CMS and the public website (Web) are two separate applications. The CMS WRITES content, Web only READS it — Web never writes to the database (except anonymous visitor analytics and form submissions, which go into their own isolated tables). This separation means a bug or slowdown in the CMS can never affect the live public site.

data.name: About_LoadBalancerBody
data.value: The public website (Web) is stateless — it keeps no session state of its own and the database is its single source of truth — so it can run behind a load balancer across multiple instances without any special setup. The CMS is different: it uses Blazor's interactive Server render mode for some components, which relies on a persistent SignalR connection ("circuit") to one specific server instance. Running more than one CMS instance behind a load balancer therefore needs either sticky sessions (the balancer always routes a given user back to the same instance) or a shared SignalR backplane (e.g. Redis) so circuits survive being routed to a different instance. In practice this rarely matters for the CMS — it's a low-concurrency internal tool — but it's worth knowing before scaling it out. This is a documentation note only; no code changes are needed unless you actually deploy multiple CMS instances.

data.name: KB_XssWarningBody
data.value: Users with the Developer role (or above) can insert raw HTML/JavaScript into a page (via GrapeJS's "Custom Code" block). This inherently carries an XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) risk — a malicious or carelessly written script could run in every visitor's browser. For this reason, this capability should only ever be granted to trusted, authorized users (see Roles and Permissions).

data.name: KB_SitemapLanguageBody
data.value: The sitemap lists every language version of a page as an entry of its own, each naming all the others. It is split into sections: each section under the default language's homepage (for example /articles) gets its own sitemap, and the translations of its pages go into the same one. Homepages, and pages that belong to no section, go into /sitemap-main.xml. Drafts, noindex pages and pages in unpublished languages are left out; a published page is listed even when its parent is a draft. The sitemap is rebuilt every two hours, and straight away when the default language changes.

data.value: Select the block and click the ▼ button on its floating toolbar to open the panel; ▲ closes it again. The ⇕ button in the top bar opens or closes every hidden panel on the page at once.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideOverlayStep2
data.value: Selecting anything inside a closed panel from the Layers panel opens it as well, and a block you have just dropped opens once so you can see what was added.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideOverlayStep3
data.value: Whether a panel is open in the editor is never saved — every page opens with everything closed, and the visitor always sees the closed state until they click.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideOverlayDetails
data.value: FAQ answers and Accordion sections are different: they are held open in the editor so they can be edited in place, and ship closed. Tick "Open at start" on a section to ship that one open.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideTemplatesTitle
data.value: Why can't I edit the header / footer on this page?

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideTemplatesIntro
data.value: Because it is a linked template: one source, shown on every page it is placed on. The page only holds a reference, so an edit made here would never reach the site. Clicking on it selects the whole template and its toolbar gives you the two things that work:

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideTemplatesStep1
data.value: The pencil opens the template itself in a new tab — edit and save there, and every page using it follows.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideTemplatesStep2
data.value: The open lock cuts the link: this page gets its own copy, editable in place. The other pages keep the template.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideTemplatesStep3
data.value: Moving, duplicating or deleting the template as a whole on this page works as with any block.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideTemplatesNote
data.value: A template inserted as a copy has none of this: it is ordinary content, and the editor only tells you when the source template has changed since.

data.name: PageEditor_SiteCodesWarning

data.name: PageEditor_SiteCodesNone

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideMultiStepTitle
data.value: How do I edit the Multi-Step Form?

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideMultiStepStep1
data.value: Once you drop the block onto the page, every step's content is visible and editable at the same time — visitors on the live site only ever see the first step, and move to the next one by clicking "Next".

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideMultiStepStep2
data.value: To edit the second (or later) step, just click directly on that step's heading, labels, or input fields on the page — no extra step needed.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormAttachments
data.value: To ask for a file, drag the "File Field" block into the form (at most 3 files, 10 MB, PDF/JPG/PNG/WebP/DOCX). Details in the Knowledge Base: File attachments on forms.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormTitle
data.value: How do I set up form actions?

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormStep1
data.value: Add a form block (Contact Form or Multi-Step Form).

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormSelectHint
data.value: To see the form's settings, select the form itself — not a field or a wrapper inside it. If you selected the wrong thing, open the Layers tab on the right and pick "Form" from the list.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormStep2
data.value: Tick "Yanıtları Kaydet" (save responses) in the Content tab — responses then show up under Forms in the CMS.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormStep3
data.value: Use "Form Name" to tell this form apart from others.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormStep4
data.value: Choose what happens after sending in "Submit Sonrası": "Mesaj Göster" (show a message), "Sayfaya Yönlendir" (go to a page) or "Pop-up Göster" (show a pop-up). With a message, you can write your own texts in "Başarı Mesajı" and "Hata Mesajı"; left empty, the default texts are used.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuideFormStep5
data.value: If you chose redirect, fill in the "Redirect URL"; if you chose pop-up, fill in the "Pop-up ID to Show" (must match the pop-up's own ID).

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingIntro
data.value: This block automatically lists the sub-pages of a category page (e.g. blog posts, products) — complete with a search box, tag filter and pagination. No code required.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingSourceStep
data.value: After placing the block, choose its "Data Source" in the Content tab: the sub-pages of the page you're on, the sub-pages of a page you pick ("Source Page"), or every published page on the site.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingCardStep
data.value: The sample card you see on the canvas (image + date + title + summary + tags) is a real, editable design — resize it, recolor it, rearrange it, or delete the parts you don't want (e.g. the date line). Once published, this ONE card is automatically duplicated for every page found and filled in with the real page's information. Use "Column Count" together with the "Grid" or "Masonry" layout to arrange cards side by side (2, 3, 4… columns) — the canvas updates instantly as you change these.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingEmptyStep
data.value: The "No results found" text under the sample card only appears to visitors when the list is genuinely empty — restyle or reword it like any other element.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingSearchStep
data.value: The search box is a real component too — style the input and button exactly like anything else. Turning off "Show Search Box" removes it entirely.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingTagStep
data.value: If you add tags to pages in the Tags tab of Page Settings, a tag list appears in this block by itself. Clicking a tag shows only the pages carrying it.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingPaginationLookStep
data.value: The pagination section has three sample elements: "«" (previous), "1" (a page number) and "»" (next). Their APPEARANCE (color, size, rounded corners, a different icon instead of an arrow, etc.) is entirely up to you — just click the link labeled "1" and design it like any other element; the system automatically reuses that same design for every page number.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingPaginationStyleStep
data.value: The "Pagination Style" setting decides WHICH page numbers are shown, and there are five ready-made formats: "Numbers only" (1 2 3 4 5), "Arrows + numbers" (« 1 2 3 »), "Shortened" (1 2 … 10), "Arrows + shortened" (« 1 2 … 10 ») and "Arrows only" (« ») for a minimal previous/next look. The appearance is always your own design — this setting only chooses which numbers get listed, and the canvas previews it instantly.

data.name: PageEditor_HelpGuidePageListingPaginationAutoHideStep
data.value: Pagination hides itself automatically when there's only one page of results — no setting needed for that.

data.name: Guide_DarkModeTitle
data.value: Dark mode / light mode — already built in

data.name: Guide_DarkModeIntro
data.value: Every site already ships with both a light and a dark palette (Site Codes → "Marka Renkleri") and a script that applies whichever the visitor's own system prefers the first time they land — nothing to add for that part, it already works.

data.name: Guide_DarkModeStep1
data.value: To let a visitor override that and switch manually, drag the "Tema Değiştirici" block (Elevare UI Kit palette) onto any page — a header or footer is the usual spot, but it works anywhere. It reads and writes the exact same setting the automatic switch does, so the two never disagree.

data.name: Guide_DarkModeStep2
data.value: Want the palette itself to look different, not just switch? Open Site Codes → "Marka Renkleri" — the light values live under :root, the dark ones under [data-theme="dark"]. Edit either one; the mechanism that switches between them stays untouched.

data.name: Guide_DarkModeWarning
data.value: This only affects blocks that read the --elevare-* variables. A block edited with a hand-picked hex color keeps that exact color and won't follow the toggle.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsIntro
data.value: The block library reads its colors from a handful of CSS custom properties instead of hardcoded hex values, so a rebrand doesn't mean editing every block by hand.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsStep1
data.value: Open Site Codes and edit the "Marka Renkleri (CSS Değişkenleri)" row.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsStep2
data.value: Change --elevare-primary, --elevare-secondary and the other values, then save.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsStep3
data.value: Blocks already on your pages switch to the new colors by themselves — no per-block editing.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsA11yBody
data.value: Two colors can look fine side by side and still be unreadable — text and its background need enough contrast between them, not just a pleasant combination. Aim for at least a 4.5:1 ratio for ordinary text (3:1 is enough for large headings). You don't need an outside tool to check it: open any page's SEO panel (the score badge, top right of the canvas) — its Accessibility section already flags every element that falls short and can point you straight to it.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsWarning
data.value: A block whose color you picked by hand in the Style tab doesn't follow the palette; it keeps the color you picked.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsTemplateTitle
data.value: The full palette, ready to paste

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsTemplateBody
data.value: Paste this into Site Codes -> "Marka Renkleri (CSS Değişkenleri)" and change the values you want. These are the defaults the site shipped with, so the same paste also puts the palette back if an edit goes wrong.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsTemplateCopyFailed
data.value: Could not copy — select the text and copy it by hand.

data.name: Guide_BrandColorsTemplateNote
data.value: Keep every line. A variable that is missing does not raise an error: each block falls back to the colour baked into its own markup, so parts of the site quietly stop following the palette. --elevare-on-primary is the one people forget — it is the text on a primary-coloured button, and leaving it out is how you end up with white on white when the primary itself is light.

data.name: Guide_TemplateLanguageIntro
data.value: A template's Language field is filtering only — it decides which templates you see in the panel, nothing more. Inserting a template never copies content across languages; it always inserts that exact template's own HTML into the page you're on.

data.name: Guide_TemplateLanguageStep1
data.value: The language filter doesn't jump to match the page you're editing, on purpose — you might want to insert a completely different template into an EN page, and an auto-switching filter would take that choice away from you.

data.name: Guide_TemplateLanguageStep2
data.value: Pages work the same way: a page's TR and EN versions are entirely separate records. A change made on TR never carries over to EN — you're always looking at that page's own copy in that one language.

data.name: Guide_TemplateLanguageWarning
data.value: Don't try to show one template in two languages by hiding/showing text with CSS classes (.lbl-tr / .lbl-en and the like) — every edit then has to be made twice and tested in both languages. For a block that carries real words — a header, a footer, anything with copy — give each language its own template instead, and set the Language field to match.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesTitle
data.value: Site Codes — how to use them

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesIntro
data.value: Site Codes is where every third-party tag and every piece of hand-written CSS/JS/HTML for the public site lives — analytics, pixels, consent banners, custom styling, anything that used to be a one-off free-text setting.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesStep1
data.value: Tool prepares the code for you — for Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, Search Console verification and Cookie consent you only paste the ID or code the provider gave you; pick "Custom code" for anything else.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesStep2
data.value: Position decides where in the page the code goes — Top of head, End of head, Start of body or End of body — and codes in the same position are added in the order you set.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesStep3
data.value: Type (Script, Style, Meta tag, Raw HTML) checks that what you wrote is that kind of code. Whatever you write in Code is added to the page exactly as-is, so it must be complete: your own <script>/<style> tags included.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesStep4
data.value: The "Live" switch on each row turns a code off without deleting it — handy for trying a tag before it goes live, or pausing one for a while.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesConsentHint
data.value: Put the cookie consent code at "Top of head" — it works by holding back other scripts, which it can only do if the browser reads it first.

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesAnalyticsConsentWarningTitle
data.value: The Google Analytics 4 preset doesn't wait for consent

data.name: Guide_SiteCodesAnalyticsConsentWarningBody
data.value: With "Google Analytics 4" as the Tool, the code runs for everyone as soon as the page loads — it does not wait for cookie consent (which can be a compliance problem under GDPR/KVKK). If tracking should only run for visitors who agree, add GA4 as "Custom code" and write the script tag as <script type="text/plain" data-category="analytics">; your consent tool turns it into a real script once the visitor accepts analytics cookies.

data.name: Guide_FaviconLogoIntro
data.value: Both are in Site Settings, under Site Identity — not in Site Codes.

data.name: Guide_FaviconLogoStep1
data.value: Go to Site Settings → Site Identity.

data.name: Guide_FaviconLogoStep2
data.value: Set Logo URL and Favicon URL by picking a file from the Media Library (or uploading a new one there first).

data.name: Guide_FaviconLogoStep3

data.name: Guide_FaviconLogoNote

data.name: Guide_SeoSettingsIntro

data.name: Guide_SeoSettingsStep3
data.value: Search engine verification (Google Search Console, for instance) isn't set here — open Site Codes, add a row, pick "Search Console verification" as the Tool and paste the code Google gave you.

data.value: Delete workflow "{0}"? This cannot be undone.

data.name: Approvals_Subtitle
data.value: Content staged behind an active workflow waits here until every required step approves it.

data.name: Approvals_LoadError
data.value: Pending approvals could not be loaded.

data.name: Backups_Subtitle
data.value: Weekly database backups, taken and verified automatically.

data.name: Backups_OffsiteTitle
data.value: These backups live on the database server

data.name: Backups_OffsiteExplanation
data.value: They protect you against a bad deployment, a wrong bulk edit or a dropped table — but not against losing the machine. Include the backup folder in the server's own off-site backup or snapshot routine.

data.name: Backups_Empty
data.value: No backups yet. Use “Back up now” to take the first one.

data.name: Backups_QueuedMessage
data.value: Backup queued. A full backup takes a few minutes — refresh the list to see it.

data.name: KB_RedirectsImportFormatBody
data.value: The file must be CSV — in Excel, use "Save As" and pick "CSV (semicolon delimited)". The first row is a header and is not read; every row after it becomes one rule. The first column is the old path (e.g. /old-page), the second is the new one. A leading "/" on either path is optional — the system normalizes it either way.

data.name: KB_RedirectsImportGoneSubtitle
data.value: What happens if I leave the new path empty?

data.name: KB_RedirectsImportGoneBody
data.value: That row's old path is treated as permanently removed and answers 410 Gone to visitors — it sends them nowhere. Use this for pages you took down with no replacement.

data.name: KB_RedirectsImportValidationSubtitle
data.value: What happens if a row is invalid?

data.name: KB_RedirectsImportValidationBody
data.value: Each row is validated on its own, exactly as if it had been typed in by hand: if the old path already exists, would create a loop, or is empty, that row is skipped and its error is listed on screen — but the other, valid rows are still created. So one import can end in partial success; the on-screen summary shows which rows did not go in.

data.name: KB_SecretsWhatBody
data.value: The "Secrets" tab on Site Settings holds credentials for systems outside the CMS itself, not the CMS's own configuration: the password for the SMTP server that sends mail, the CAPTCHA provider's secret key that guards public forms against spam, and the access keys needed to upload images to an S3-compatible bucket/CDN. The CMS runs fine without any of these set — the matching integration just stays off.

data.name: KB_SecretsWhySeparateSubtitle
data.value: Why is this kept apart from the rest of Site Settings?

data.name: KB_SecretsWhySeparateBody
data.value: Every field on the regular Site Settings screen (site name, CDN base URL, the CAPTCHA site key) is already public or at least not sensitive — which is why nothing there is encrypted. Secrets are real credentials instead, kept in their own table and encrypted with the same key ring the CMS already uses to protect sessions. Once saved, a secret is never shown back in plain text — only whether it's set; changing one means typing a new value, and removing one means using the separate "Remove" link.

data.name: KB_SecretsWhoBody
data.value: Only SuperAdmin, by default — not even Admin sees it automatically, because this is more of an infrastructure-level concern than day-to-day site administration. If needed, grant the "Manage infrastructure secrets" permission to any role from Roles and Permissions.

data.name: KB_SecretsFileSubtitle
data.value: How does this relate to appsettings.json / .env?

data.name: KB_SecretsFileBody
data.value: Both work, and the database wins. Leave a field here empty (never entered) and the system keeps using whatever is in appsettings.json/.env — nothing breaks on an existing install. Enter and save a value here and it overrides the appsettings.json/.env equivalent from then on.

data.name: KB_SecretsRestartSubtitle
data.value: Does it take effect right away?

data.name: KB_SecretsRestartBody
data.value: Yes — every field here, including which storage provider is active, applies to the very next request with no restart. The one exception is the CAPTCHA secret key: telling the public site about the new value is a network call to a separate process, so it can lag a second or two behind the save. If that call fails (the site was down, for instance), the save still succeeds and the CMS reports it — save it again once the site is reachable.

data.name: KB_TemplatesIntro
data.value: A template is a piece of page content — a header, a footer, a WhatsApp button — kept once and placed on many pages. How it is placed on a page decides what editing it later means.

data.name: KB_TemplatesLinkedBody
data.value: The page holds only a reference. Visitors always see the template's current content, and so does the page editor: edit the template once and every page follows — no re-save. That is also why it is read-only on the page: an edit made inside it there would be saved, never shown, and silently gone the next time the page was opened. Clicking anywhere on a linked template selects it as one piece; its toolbar offers two things — the pencil opens the template editor in a new tab, the open lock cuts the link and turns that instance into an ordinary copy. Moving, cloning or deleting the template as a whole still works.

data.name: KB_TemplatesCopyBody
data.value: The content itself is copied onto the page and is ordinary content from then on — edit it freely. Linked templates inside it (a header, a footer) are not copied: they stay linked and follow the rest of the site. The copy remembers which template it came from and when: if the template's own content changes later, a note appears above the editor — when it was copied, when the template changed, "Open template" and "don't show again" for that change. It never pulls the change in. To get back on the template, delete the copy and insert the template again.

data.name: KB_TemplatesWhichBody
data.value: Linked for anything that must be identical everywhere — the site's header, footer, floating buttons. A copy when one page needs its own variation of it. Cutting a link is one-way.

data.name: KB_FormAttachmentsBody
data.value: Drag the "File Field" block (Form & Interaction category) into a form and a visitor can attach a CV, a photo or a document. On the block you set the label, the field name, the accepted kinds (documents, images or both), multiple selection and whether it is required. When a submission arrives, the Forms screen lists its files under "Attachments"; a click downloads the file.

data.name: KB_FormAttachmentsLimitsBody
data.value: At most 3 files per form, 10 MB each; only PDF, JPG, PNG, WebP and DOCX. The kind is decided by the file's content, not its name — a program named "cv.pdf" is refused, a JPEG named "photo.pdf" is stored as the JPEG it is. One file over a limit refuses the whole submission and the visitor is told why ("A file is larger than 10 MB"), so a form is never reported "sent" with an attachment missing. CAPTCHA and the request limit apply here too.

data.name: KB_FormAttachmentsWhereSubtitle
data.value: Where they live, who can open them

data.name: KB_FormAttachmentsWhereBody
data.value: Files are written to the database beside the submission, not to the media library: they have no public address, cannot be guessed and opened, and go into backups with the submission. Only users with the "View form submissions" permission can download them; the browser always downloads, never opens them inside the CMS. Deleting a submission deletes its attachments.

data.name: KB_SiteCodesPerPageTitle
data.value: Switching a site code off on one page

data.name: KB_SiteCodesPerPageBody
data.value: Site codes run on every page. To keep one off a single page — the chat widget on a landing page, for instance — open the page in the editor, go to the "Site Codes" tab in Page Settings and tick the code. It is saved with the page and applies on the public site, in previews and in the editor. The tab lists names and positions only; the code itself is still edited on the Site Codes screen. It is exclusion only: a page that needs code of its own uses the custom-code block.

data.name: KB_SiteCodesPerPageWarning
data.value: Careful with the base stylesheets and the consent banner: switching a stylesheet off can break the page's look, switching the consent banner off can run trackers without consent on that page.

data.name: KB_LighthouseTitle
data.value: Lighthouse: what it flags, and whose job it is

data.name: KB_LighthouseIntro
data.value: Lighthouse (Chrome DevTools → Lighthouse) scores a page on performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO. Most of what it flags on an Elevare site falls into one of three buckets: content — yours to change in the editor or the media library; platform — handled by the CMS and the site automatically; server — the web server in front of the site.

data.name: KB_LighthouseImagesBody
data.value: The biggest lever. Every image uploaded from now on gets WebP copies and resized versions (480–1920 px) automatically, and the public page serves the right one for the space it fills — images uploaded earlier get theirs the first time the CMS starts after this update. Uploads over 2560 pixels are brought down to that size before they are stored, and JPEGs are re-compressed with no visible loss. What is still yours: every image defaults to "Lazy", so set only the first picture at the top of the page to "Eager" (it gets preloaded with high priority), and set a favicon from an image in the library — the CMS makes the 32/48/180/192/512 px set from it. Proportions too: in an image's Size field, with the lock on, type the width and the height fills in from the file's own ratio (or the other way round); when the two disagree the field warns and "Fit to ratio" repairs it. The SEO analysis also lists images shown at the wrong proportions — the counterpart of Lighthouse's "incorrect aspect ratio" finding.

data.name: KB_LighthouseContrastSubtitle
data.value: Colour contrast ("Background and foreground colors do not have a sufficient contrast ratio")

data.name: KB_LighthouseContrastBody
data.value: Almost always the brand palette's muted text colour (--elevare-muted) on the page background: it needs at least 4.5:1 for normal text. Pick it in the Site Codes palette against your background — a darker grey costs nothing in a light theme — and check with any contrast checker. The seeded palette passes; a custom one is yours to verify.

data.name: KB_LighthouseButtonsSubtitle
data.value: Buttons and touch targets ("Buttons do not have an accessible name", "Touch targets")

data.name: KB_LighthouseButtonsBody
data.value: A button whose text was removed, leaving only an icon, has no name for a screen reader. The Button, Mega Menu and Side Panel blocks now put the last label back as an aria-label when the text is gone; the Aria Label field in the settings panel lets you set a better one. Slider dots are 24 px touch targets now — both take effect the next time the page is saved.

data.name: KB_LighthouseThirdPartyBody
data.value: A consent banner's stylesheet loaded from a CDN at the top of the page holds the first paint until the CDN answers. The Cookie Consent preset in Site Codes now splits a paste into a script row and a stylesheet row that loads without blocking, and preconnects to the CDN; re-save the consent snippet through the preset to get this. The script itself is left synchronous on purpose — a consent tool has to run before the trackers it blocks.

data.name: KB_LighthouseServerBody
data.value: Not the application: the reverse proxy in front of it (nginx, Caddy, IIS) speaks HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 to visitors. With nginx it is the http2 flag on the TLS listen line; the containers behind it need no change.

data.name: KB_RestoreBody
data.value: Restoring is deliberately not a button in this CMS — it overwrites the live database and cannot be undone. Run it yourself, from the command line, when you have decided it is the right move. Take a fresh backup first: the restore destroys everything written since the backup you are restoring.

data.name: KB_RestoreCommands1
data.value: # 1. Stop the apps so nothing writes while restoring

data.name: KB_RestoreCommands2
data.value: # 2. Drop and recreate the database, then restore the dump into it # (run from inside the cms container, or anywhere with pg_restore and network # access to the db service — the backup file lives in the db-backups volume, # mounted into cms at /app/Backups)

data.name: KB_RestoreCommandsFileHint
data.value: file shown on the Backups page

data.name: KB_RestoreAfterNote
data.value: After restoring, clear the site cache (Cache page) and restart the CMS so no stale snapshot survives the swap.

data.name: KB_LanguageTitle
data.value: Language on Pages vs. Language on Templates

data.name: KB_LanguagePagesBody
data.value: A page's language is a real structural link, not a label. Pages that share a Page Group are translations of each other, and that link is what everything else reads from: the sitemap's hreflang alternates, the Language Switcher block, and the URL itself — the default language sits at the root (/about), every other language gets its own prefix (/en/about). Assign a page to a language and it's wired into all of that automatically. Changing the default language changes every page's address: old addresses redirect to the new ones, and links in pages, share addresses and structured data are updated to the new addresses.

data.name: KB_LanguageTemplatesBody
data.value: A template's language field is a different thing entirely — it's informational only, there purely to help you find and organize templates, and it filters the template list and the insert-into-page panel. Setting it does not link a template to a page or a language the way a page's own language does. It matters in practice because a template carrying real words (a header's nav labels, for instance) only makes sense in one language — so a header with actual text needs one genuine template per language, each inserted into the matching pages, rather than one template trying to speak both languages at once.

data.name: KB_ResponsiveImagesWhatBody
data.value: Sending a phone a 1920-pixel photograph for a spot that is 400 pixels wide downloads far more than needed — the page is slower, the visitor's data is wasted. The fix is to keep the same picture ready at several sizes and let the browser pick the one that fits its screen ("srcset" in HTML terms). Elevare does all of it: the one thing it asks of you is to upload the picture once.

data.name: KB_ResponsiveImagesHowBody
data.value: From the JPEG, PNG or WebP you upload, a "master" is kept: scaled down if its long edge is over 2560 pixels, turned the right way up per the phone's orientation tag, and — for a JPEG — re-compressed with no visible loss (a 2 MB photo typically comes down to a few hundred KB). Next to the master, WebP and JPEG/PNG copies at 480/640/960/1440/1920 pixels and a full-size WebP are generated; the site serves each visitor the one that fits. The library still shows one row — the copies belong to the file, and are deleted with it. Images uploaded before this update go through the same process the first time the CMS starts. GIF, SVG and ICO are left alone.

data.name: KB_ResponsiveImagesAltBody
data.value: The title and alt text you enter at upload are written to the file itself. When you add an image from the picker in the page editor, the alt text is filled in automatically — there is nothing to type. If you wrote an alt text yourself the system does not touch it, and an alt you deliberately left empty (right for a decorative image) is preserved too.

data.name: KB_ResponsiveImagesPasteSubtitle
data.value: What if I paste a link by hand?

data.name: KB_ResponsiveImagesPasteBody
data.value: It still works. If you copy a link from the library into a Custom Code block or a hand-written tag, the site finds that address in the library when it publishes the page and fills in what is missing itself (the WebP and smaller sizes, alt text, width/height). Whichever way you add an image the result is the same. Still, prefer the picker in the editor: it is the only route where you see and confirm the alt text as you go.

data.name: KB_ResponsiveImagesCompressionBody
data.value: A sensibly sized original: 1920–2560 pixels wide is enough almost anywhere; there is no point uploading a 5000-pixel phone photo as it is, it will be brought down to 2560 anyway. JPEG (photographs) or PNG (logos, transparency) is all you need — converting to WebP is not your job. If you want an entirely different crop on phones, upload that as a separate image and use it separately on the page.

data.name: KB_TwoLetterCodeNameBody
data.value: The field is called "two-letter" but actually allows up to 5 characters — the name comes from the most common examples (tr, en), not a technical limit. This field is the language's single identity on the site: the URL prefix (/en/...), every page's hreflang alternates, the sitemap's section split, structured data's inLanguage field, and <html lang> all derive from it directly.

data.name: KB_TwoLetterCodeLengthBody
data.value: When creating a language, this field can hold not just a short code like "tr" but a region-qualified one like "en-gb" (fits within 5 characters). You cannot create two languages with the same two-letter code — the system blocks that automatically — but "en-gb" and "en-us" are different strings, so both can be created without conflict.

data.name: KB_TwoLetterCodeRegionBody
data.value: The concrete benefit of adding a region: if you define British and American English as separate languages (en-gb / en-us), each one automatically gets its own correct URL prefix (/en-gb/..., /en-us/...), its own correct hreflang value, and its own og:locale meta tag (en_GB / en_US) — since all of it derives from this one field, there is nowhere else you need to enter region information separately.

data.name: KB_SkipLinkBody
data.value: Every page starts with an invisible "Skip to content" link that appears on the first Tab press — it lets a keyboard or screen-reader visitor jump straight past the header/nav that repeats on every page and into the page's own content (WCAG 2.4.1). It isn't a hidden decoy in the source; it is genuinely the first focusable thing in the body, ahead of the header/nav markup and even ahead of Site Codes' own Body Start rows. Its visibility comes from the .skip-link rules inside the "Critical CSS" Site Codes row — if that row is deleted or edited away, the link can become visually invisible even when focused (it stays in the DOM and reachable by keyboard either way).

data.name: PageEditor_StructuredDataOpenEmpty
data.value: No structured data — open to create

data.name: StructuredData_EmptyPreview
data.value: No structured data yet. Use "Build Draft" on the right to generate a starting point from your site and page details.

data.name: StructuredData_BuildDraftHint
data.value: The draft is generated from your organisation details in Site Settings, the page's own data and its parent chain. If the page has an FAQ block, its questions are added too. Rebuilding discards edits you made by hand.

data.name: StructuredData_PasteHint
data.value: Paste a JSON-LD node from the JSON builder panel or anywhere else. A single object, an array of several nodes, or a whole @graph document all work.

data.value: Analytics, cookie consent, verification and other third-party code. Each one is named, can be switched off on its own, and is checked before it reaches a page.

data.name: SiteCode_BrandColorNoticeBody

data.name: SiteCode_BrandColorNoticeLink

data.name: SiteCode_FieldNameHint

data.name: SiteCode_FieldPresetInput

data.name: Seo_Subtitle
data.value: How search engines and AI tools see the site. All three areas here apply site-wide; an individual page's own title and description live in the page editor.

data.name: Seo_TabHint_General

data.name: Seo_TabHint_Robots

data.name: Seo_TabHint_Llms

data.name: Seo_FieldMetaDescriptionHint

data.name: Seo_LlmsNotServed

data.name: Guide_PageSubtitle
data.value: Step-by-step instructions for the blocks and tools in the page builder.

data.name: About_WhatIsElevareBody
data.value: Elevare is a content management system built so small and mid-sized businesses can run their own website without needing technical knowledge. It brings a drag-and-drop page builder, multilingual content, and approval workflows together in one admin panel.

data.name: About_WhatIsElevarePoint1
data.value: Build pages from ready-made blocks, no code required

data.name: About_WhatIsElevarePoint2
data.value: Manage content in multiple languages with automatic hreflang tags

data.name: About_WhatIsElevarePoint3
data.value: Workflows that route content through an approval chain before it goes live

data.name: About_WhatIsElevarePoint4
data.value: Per-page SEO, structured data, and settings for search engines and AI tools like robots.txt/llms.txt

data.name: About_DeveloperBody
data.value: Elevare is a personal project where I designed and built every layer myself, from architecture to authorization to infrastructure. I took it on to push past the mid-level plateau, go deeper into system design, and take end-to-end ownership of something real. It's as much a lab as a product — every module got my full attention, a place to push what I know and how I work to their limit. If you run into a bug along the way, let me know at oguzhan.karaguzel@gmail.com — I'll happily fix it.

data.name: PageEditor_SeoRobotsIntro
data.value: How this page behaves in search results. The page stays publicly reachable — these are requests made to search engines, nothing more.

data.name: PageEditor_SeoNoIndexHint
data.value: Visitors can still reach the page, but it will not appear in Google results. The usual case is a paid-campaign landing page: the same content should not compete with itself for its own traffic.

data.name: PageEditor_SeoNoFollowHint
data.value: Links on this page pass no ranking signal. Independent of noindex — either can be on without the other.

data.name: PageEditor_SeoNoIndexWarning
data.value: This page will not appear in search results, and it will be left out of the sitemap.

data.name: PageKind_Hint
data.value: So anyone on the team can tell at a glance what a page is. CMS-only — never shown to visitors, never sent to search engines, no effect on how the site looks. It makes the list and the filters useful: you can ask for things like 'landing pages with no structured data'.

data.name: Pages_FiltersIntro
data.value: Picking more than one filter narrows the list to pages that match all of them. For example, to find pages with no structured data that are not landing pages: tick 'No structured data' and select every type except Landing Page.

data.name: Pages_FilterKindHint
data.value: With none selected you get every type. To leave a type out, select the others instead of it.

data.name: Pages_FilterSignalsHint
data.value: Only pages carrying every condition you pick are listed.

data.name: SiteHealth_PublicSiteErroring_Title

data.name: SiteHealth_PublicSiteErroring_Detail

data.name: SiteHealth_PublicSiteSlow_Detail

data.name: Profile_SectionPasswordHint
data.value: The new password must be at least 8 characters. We ask for your current one even though you are signed in, so an unattended screen cannot lock you out of your own account.
